// src/compat/util/toNumber.ts
/**
* Converts `value` to a number.
*
* Unlike `Number()`, this function returns `NaN` for symbols.
*
* @param value - The value to convert.
* @returns Returns the number.
*
* @example
* toNumber(3.2); // => 3.2
* toNumber(Number.MIN_VALUE); // => 5e-324
* toNumber(Infinity); // => Infinity
* toNumber('3.2'); // => 3.2
* toNumber(Symbol.iterator); // => NaN
* toNumber(NaN); // => NaN
*/
function toNumber(value) {
	if (isSymbol(value)) return NaN;
	return Number(value);
}
export { toNumber };

I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks under the project's strict settings. I couldn't compare bundle size against the original, because lodash isn't installed. The original `src/module.ts` fails to bundle and fails type checking for that reason.

The installed es-toolkit is 1.53.2. I read the declarations in `node_modules`:

| Function | es-toolkit replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pick(row, ['id','name'])` | `pick` from `es-toolkit` | Same call shape. |
| `sumBy(rows, 'age')` | `sumBy` from `es-toolkit` | The main entry takes only a function, not a property name. I added the small adapter `r => r.age`. |
| `toNumber(text)` | `toNumber` from `es-toolkit/compat` | The main entry has no `toNumber`, so this comes from compat. |

The compat `toNumber` returns `NaN` for symbols and otherwise calls `Number(value)`. I didn't run it against lodash. On the stated string inputs (digits, `.`, signs, spaces, `e`, `x`) it should match, because lodash's special cases (binary and octal prefixes, bad hex) can't occur in that alphabet. Both give 0 for an empty string and `NaN` for unreadable text.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 267 bytes (min+gzip) and 101 bytes of own code. No lodash import is left.
